'''John G. Hartnett''' (born 24 March 1953 in [[Manjimup]], Western Australia), is an Australian [[young Earth creationist]] and [[cosmologist]]. He has been active with [[Creation Ministries International]] and is known for his opposition to the [[Big Bang]] theory<ref name="ScienceNetwork"/> and criticism of the [[dark matter]] and [[dark energy]] hypotheses.<ref name="ScienceNetwork"/>

He received both his BSc (Hons) (1973) and PhD with distinction (2001) from the School of Physics at the [[University of Western Australia]] (UWA). He currently works as a Research Fellow at the [[University of Adelaide]], South Australia. He has published more than 200 papers in scientific journals, book chapters and conference proceedings, holds one patent,<ref name="UWA">{{cite web|title=UWA Staff Profile: Professor John Hartnett|publisher=[[University of Western Australia]]|quote=Thesis: 1; Edited book: 1; Refereed Book Chapters: 9; Refereed Journal Papers: 105; Refereed Conference Papers: 3; Conference Papers: 88; Patents: 1; Web of Science Citation Report: Total citations: 924; Average: 9.06; h-index: 15|url=http://www.uwa.edu.au/people/john.hartnett|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110810151832/http://www.uwa.edu.au/people/John.Hartnett|archive-date=10 August 2011}}</ref> works on the development of ultra-stable cryocooled sapphire oscillators<ref>{{cite journal   |title= Ultra-low-phase-noise cryocooled microwave dielectric-sapphire-resonator oscillators   |doi= 10.1063/1.4709479  |volume= 100   |issue= 18   |journal= Applied Physics Letters   |pages= 183501   |arxiv= 1202.2206   |bibcode= 2012ApPhL.100r3501H   |year= 2012   |last1= Hartnett   |first1= John G.   |last2= Nand   |first2= Nitin R.   |last3= Lu   |first3= Chuan   |s2cid= 118435663 }}{{Dead link|date=February 2020 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> and participated on a Sapphire Clock Ensemble project ([[Atomic Clock]] Ensemble in [[Space Mission]]) run by the [[European Space Agency]].<ref>{{cite web|title= University news|url=http://www.news.uwa.edu.au/content/dr-mohri-visit|publisher=[[University of Western Australia]]}}</ref> He also has written articles for several creationist journals<ref>{{cite web|title= Dr John Hartnett, Physics, Cosmology (Australia), Biography |url=http://creation.com/dr-john-hartnett-cv|access-date= 2011-11-18|publisher=[[Creation Ministries International]]}}</ref> and, according to [[Creation Ministries International]], Hartnett "believes that God is the real creator of the universe as the Bible says."<ref>{{cite web |url=http://creation.com/starlight-time-and-the-new-physics-tour-with-dr-john-hartnett |title=Starlight, Time and the New Physics tour with Dr John Hartnett |work=creation.com |date=2012 |access-date=23 February 2012 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090426112952/http://creation.com/starlight-time-and-the-new-physics-tour-with-dr-john-hartnett |archive-date=26 April 2009 }}</ref>

==Research interests==
His research interests include ultra low-noise radar and ultra high stability [[cryogenic]] microwave [[oscillator]]s and clocks based on a pure single-crystal [[sapphire]] [[resonator]]s. Applications for the latter are to provide low noise [[local oscillator]]s to atomic physics labs, time and frequency atomic fountain standards, and [[very high frequency]] [[VLBI]] (Very-Long-Baseline-Interferometry) radio-astronomy. The terrestrial clock technology co-developed by him is claimed to be the most stable in the universe, with Hartnett et al. stating that it outperformed the stability of signals generated by [[pulsar]]s (rotating [[neutron stars]] that produce highly periodic bursts of [[radio wave]]s; such astronomical sources are then used as natural clocks e.g. for tests of physics).<ref>{{cite web|title=Where Is the Best Clock in the Universe? |work=arXiv blog|publisher=MIT Technology Review |url= http://www.technologyreview.com/blog/arxiv/25008/|quote= The widespread belief that pulsars are the best clocks in the universe is wrong, say physicists.|access-date= 2011-11-18}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|first=John |last=Hartnett |author2=Luiten, Andre |title=Colloquium: Comparison of Astrophysical and Terrestrial Frequency Standards |year=2011|quote= We have re-analyzed the stability of pulse arrival times from pulsars and white dwarfs using several analysis tools for measuring the noise characteristics of sampled time and frequency data. We show that the best terrestrial artificial clocks substantially exceed the performance of astronomical sources as time-keepers in terms of accuracy (as defined by cesium primary frequency standards) and stability. ...we show that detailed accuracy evaluations of modern terrestrial clocks imply that these new clocks are likely to have a stability better than any astronomical source up to comparison times of at least hundreds of years. |pages= 1–9|doi= 10.1103/RevModPhys.83.1|volume=83|issue=1 |journal=Reviews of Modern Physics |arxiv= 1004.0115|bibcode = 2011RvMP...83....1H |s2cid=118396798 }}</ref> Further on, he is interested in the development of [[Cryocooler|cryocooled]] CSO [[resonators]], detection of WISPs using low noise microwave techniques, tests of the fundamental theories of physics, such as [[special relativity|special]] and [[general relativity]], measurement of drift in fundamental constants<ref>{{cite web|first= John|last= Hartnett|title= Quantized quasar redshifts in a creationist cosmology |url= http://creation.com/images/pdfs/tj/j18_2/j18_2_105-113.pdf|access-date=2011-11-19}}</ref> and their [[cosmological]] implications and [[Physical cosmology|cosmology]] and [[Large-scale structure of the cosmos|the large scale structure of the universe]].<ref name="UWA"/><ref>Hartnett, John, chapter in {{cite book|last= Carmeli|first= Moshe |title= Relativity: modern large-scale spacetime structure of the cosmos|publisher= World Scientific Publishing|location=London, UK| page= 363|isbn= 978-981-281-375-6|date=2008|url= https://books.google.com/books?id=tZ2ilHyrkGUC&dq=Hartnett+redshifts&pg=PA363|access-date= 2011-11-18}}</ref> He is also part of a team of scientists who are building liquid helium-cooled oscillators used by sapphire clocks for the National Metrology Institute of Japan in Tsukuba, Japan.<ref name = "abc.au2008"/>

According to [[Moshe Carmeli]], Professor of Theoretical Physics at Ben Gurion University in Beer Sheva, Israel,<ref>{{cite web|title=Moshe Carmeli|publisher=Ben Gurion University|url=http://physics.bgu.ac.il/HOMEPAGES/FACULTY/Carmeli/main.html|access-date=2011-11-27|archive-date=26 April 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120426005146/http://physics.bgu.ac.il/HOMEPAGES/FACULTY/Carmeli/main.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> Hartnett asserted in his theory that there is no need to assume the existence of [[dark matter]] in the universe.<ref>{{cite book|first=Moshe|last=Carmeli|author-link=Moshe Carmeli|title=Cosmological relativity: the special and general theories of the structure|publisher=World Scientific Publishing Co.|location=Danvers, MA, USA|date=2006|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=GS-exC2S_V0C&dq=John+Hartnett+cosmology&pg=PP7|isbn=981-270-075-7|quote=It was shown by Dr. John G. Hartnett that there is no need to assume the existence of dark matter in the universe. |access-date=2011-11-25}}</ref>

==Publications==
John Hartnett is the author of the book ''"Starlight, Time and the New Physics"'' (2007).<ref name="starlight">{{cite book| last = Hartnett| first = John| title = Starlight, Time and the New Physics| publisher = Creation Ministries International| date = 2007| isbn = 978-0-949906-68-7|page=34|quote='Dark Matter' -today's 'fudge' factor; Technical Appendices: App.1: The large scale structure of the universe does not need 'dark' matter or 'dark' energy; App.6: Light-travel-time problem solved}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last=Hopkins|first=Amanda|title=Creation vs Evolution debate on GOD TV|url=http://www.theway.co.uk/feature.php?id=8521&this=Creation_vs_Evolution__debate_on_GOD_TV|publisher=The Way|access-date=18 November 2011}}</ref> and co-author of the book ''"Dismantling the Big Bang"''.<ref name="ScienceNetwork">{{cite web|title=Big bang or bulldust?|url=http://www.sciencealert.com.au/features/20080812-18554.html|date=7 December 2008|publisher=ScienceAlert|author=ScienceNetwork WA|quote=A fundamental problem with big bang theory is the weakness of the gravitational force between stars and galaxies. 'Dark' matter – which has never been detected – is needed to explain why so much of the universe (98 percent) is missing, or cannot be seen.|access-date=18 November 2011|archive-date=7 April 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120407031705/http://www.sciencealert.com.au/features/20080812-18554.html}}</ref><ref name="Dismantling">{{cite book| last1 = Hartnett| first1 = John| first2 = Alex | last2 = Williams | title = Dismantling the Big Bang| publisher = Master Books| date = 2005 |at = Cover| isbn = 978-0-89051-437-5 |quote=As a way of explaining the universe we see, big-bang theory doesn't work. Not only does it lack a credible and consistent mechanism, but even given the credit of every possible doubt, the best it can produce is an expanding cloud of gas.}}</ref>
